title: Recipient List (v1)
description:
One published version of the Recipient List: the organisations that receive what the fees account passes on, each assigned to one of the movement's seven published categories (ops decision D33, 2026-09-06).

WHAT IT IS. What is passed on goes DIRECTLY, from the fees account, to the public-benefit organisations on this list, in the shares the published allocation rule produces for the month. There is no intermediary: no umbrella, no pooled fund, no earmark instruction, no handling fee. The board usually aims for about ten to fifteen organisations anywhere in the world. That is a non-binding target, not a rule, so this schema enforces no range: a removal for cause takes effect at once, and a contract that cannot express the true state is worse than none.

THE LEGAL INSTRUMENT IS THE BOARD'S PUBLISHED LIST, NOT THIS FILE. The Recipient List is kept by the board under statutes Art. 7, outside the statutes: it is not a statutes annex, and a change to it is never a statutes amendment. The founding list is adopted by the board at its constituting meeting, and its first publication counts as the thirty days' public notice for the entries on it. This artifact is the list's machine-readable form, which is why `x-psn.authoritative` is false. Where the two disagree the published list governs and the divergence is a defect to report.

CHANGES ARE PROSPECTIVE. An addition or a removal takes effect for months AFTER thirty days' public notice (`noticeGivenAt`, `effectiveFrom`). A removal for cause — for instance a sanctions hit or loss of registration — takes effect at once, is published with its ground, and the removed recipient's share for that month goes to the other recipients of its category (D33 item 3). There is no open self-registration: every addition meets statutes Art. 7(2) and the Recipient Rules and is a board decision, minuted and published, even where an organisation proposed itself; no recipient is ever added by free text or on a payer's or a contributor's nomination alone.

THE FLOOR IS IN THE STATUTES; THE DETAILS ARE IN THE RECIPIENT RULES. Statutes Art. 7(2) sets the minimum every recipient meets, and that floor may only be tightened: it is constituted under the law of its country as a not-for-profit organisation with a charitable or public-benefit purpose in one of the seven categories, and a newly founded organisation is not excluded; it may lawfully receive a transfer from a Swiss association under the law that applies to it; it is not the target of sanctions that apply to the Association and is not seated in a jurisdiction the FATF calls for action on; it is not controlled by any member, board member, employee or contractor of the Association, or by a person close to one, and gives no such person a personal benefit; and it is paid only into a bank account in its own name that the Association has verified. The details of the checks are set by the Recipient Rules, which the board issues and changes with publication: they may add further requirements and remove them again, but never fall below the floor. So this schema holds constant only what the floor makes constant — payment by bank transfer into a verified account, never in cash or crypto-assets (`standard.bankTransferOnly`), and the declaration of independence (`standard.independenceDeclared`) — and carries the rest as references into the recipient file, because a validator can prove that the evidence was recorded and only a human can prove that it is true. Years of accounts, an audit, a published address and a website are not requirements: `standard.accountsYears`, `address` and `website` are recorded where they exist and are never a condition of listing.

NO REAL ORGANISATION IS NAMED BEFORE THE BOARD ADOPTS AND PUBLISHES THE LIST. A sample dataset marks every entry `sample: true` and its names say so; nothing renders a recipient as listed on the strength of a fixture.

x-psn.phase: P-M3 (producer). No list has been adopted: the board adopts the founding list at its constituting meeting and publishes it as the Recipient List, kept outside the statutes, and no transfer is made before an adopted list is published.
x-psn.artifactPath: no path in the FS-00 §6.2 catalogue yet — deliberately deferred; the list is the board's published, versioned Recipient List, kept outside the statutes, and is rendered on the causes and transparency pages. The published path is fixed when FS-00 §6.2 adopts this artifact.
x-psn.producer: the operator, from the recipient files, on a board decision that is minuted and published · P-M3: the `recipients` table, published by `jobs.ledger-publish`
consumers: cost-support.v1 transfers and ledger `disburse` rows, which resolve their `recipientId` against the version in force
fsRefs: FS-07 amendment banner (D33 items 1–3 — the `recipients` table at P-M3)

version.description: This list version's own published token — the version cited by every month that transferred under it (URS TRN-024 publishes the Recipient List version in force). The token shape follows `scheduleVersion`, the contract set's other published version on a money-bearing reference (URS ENG-084), so a reader meets one form rather than two.

status.description: `adopted` means this version was adopted by the board, minuted and published as the Recipient List, which the board keeps outside the statutes and which is never a statutes annex; `draft` means it was not, and no transfer is ever made against a draft. The distinction is in the artifact because the honesty rule needs it in the artifact: a page cannot tell an adopted list from a proposal by looking at the recipients.

effectiveFrom.description: The first month this version governs. Changes are prospective: a version that adds or removes a recipient takes effect for months after thirty days' public notice (D33 item 3). A removal for cause is the one immediate change, and its recipient carries `removedAt` and `removalGround`.

noticeGivenAt.description: When the public notice for this version was given, at least thirty days before `effectiveFrom` (D33 item 3). NULL, and required rather than optional, for the two cases where no separate notice is given: the first adopted list, whose first publication itself counts as the thirty days' public notice for the entries on it, so its `effectiveFrom` lies at least thirty days after that publication; and a removal for cause, which takes effect at once. In an audit a missing key and an explicit null must not be distinguishable — the same reasoning `ct-segment.v1` gives its nullable `ref`.

adoptedAt.description: The date of the decision that adopted this version. Every addition and every removal is a board decision, minuted and published (D33 item 3).

decisionRef.description: The published minute of that decision.

standardUrl.description: Where the Recipient Rules are published: the board's rules that set the details of the checks above the floor of statutes Art. 7(2). The floor may only be tightened; the board changes the Rules with publication, never below the floor. The member keeps its D33 item 2 name, and the text a reader checks a recipient against is a published document, not a paraphrase in a schema.

categories.description: The movement's seven published categories (statutes Art. 7; D33 item 1: the seven stay, and a 'category fund' is from now on nothing but the basket of listed recipients in that category). All seven are carried in every version, including one whose recipients have all been removed for cause, because the menu is the movement's and not the list's. EXACTLY ONE ENTRY PER SLUG, enforced: seven items, and one `contains` clause per slug of `$defs.categorySlug`. `uniqueItems` would not do this job — on an array of objects it compares whole objects, so seven entries all slugged `health` with distinct names would pass it, and a published version could claim seven categories while six of the movement's seven were silently absent.

fundId.description: The `cat-{slug}` form the ledger's `categoryFundId` carries, recorded so the two vocabularies resolve to each other without a lookup table.

recipients.description: The listed organisations. The board usually aims for about ten to fifteen — a non-binding target, not a rule, so no range is enforced here; a removal for cause also takes effect at once, and the published state must remain expressible. Each entry carries its own evidence under statutes Art. 7(2) and the Recipient Rules, and the category it is assigned to.

shareRule.description: How a category's amount for a month is divided among the listed recipients OF THAT CATEGORY. DECIDED (ops decision D40 item 7, 2026-09-14; statutes Art. 8(2)): equal shares per active listed recipient, apportioned by largest remainder with ties broken by list order; a different share may be set per recipient on the List itself. Since ops decision D43 (2026-09-15; statutes Art. 8(1), (2) and (4)) the equal split applies to the REST of the category's amount: advisory designations by the persons who administer a repository or by its contributors, and the board's allocation key for shares nobody designated or that were expressly left to the Association, may name an active listed recipient and an amount, and that recipient receives the amount so determined before the rest is split. The allocation key is adopted and published before the month it applies to and changes only for later months. Note what this rule is NOT: it does not touch how much each CATEGORY receives (that is the allocation rule of FS-07 — attribution by the lane and scope each buyer paid for (ops decision D42) and the routing hierarchy), and it does not touch the annual cap on direct costs, which URS §21 OPEN-05 owns.

mode.description: `equal-per-recipient-in-category`: every listed recipient of a category carries the same share of that category's amount, which is what the sample dataset already assumes. One value today; a second value is added only by a recorded decision.

rounding.description: Largest remainder, the contract set's only apportionment rule (FS-07 FS07-030): quotas, then floors, then the remaining minor units one each in descending fractional-remainder order. Exactness holds by construction — the shares sum to the category's amount and no sub-centime dust exists.

tiebreak.description: The stated ascending stable key FS07-030 requires: the order of `recipients[]` in this published version. Publishing the tiebreak is what makes the apportionment reproducible by a reader rather than merely correct.

status.description: `proposed` until the operator confirms the rule; the value is part of the artifact so a page can say which it is. It flips to `decided` only when a dated decision says so.

note.description: The published wording of the rule, and what happens to a removed recipient's share for the month it was removed in: it goes to the other recipients of its category (D33 item 3).
Version-level narrative — what changed against the previous version and why, in the words a reader can check against the published minute.

categorySlug.description: The movement's seven published public-benefit categories (statutes Art. 7; ops decision D33 item 1). The menu is PUBLISHED in `category-menu.v1.json` (`$defs.slug`, with `examples/category-menu.v1.example.json` as the menu itself); the enum here is a copy of it. Every schema in this set must validate on its own after a single download, so none may `$ref` another — which means a shared vocabulary can only be carried as copies, and `npm run check:menu` asserts every copy is identical to the published one, so a copy cannot fork at the next amendment. Fields that constrain the vocabulary by PATTERN rather than by enum name the published menu instead: `ledger-row.v1.categoryFundId`, `ledger-export.v1`'s export-row `categoryFundId`, `cost-support.v1.transfers[].category`, and `purpose-yml.v1`'s own `categorySlug`, which stays a pattern on purpose because a manifest is untrusted repository content whose unknown slugs are rejected field by field at parse time. A category that is not on this list would be a fabricated fact about where money goes: free-text categories and free-text recipients are forbidden outright.

recipientId.description: Platform-minted ULID, `rcp_` prefix, lowercase Crockford base32 — the same identifier the ledger's `disburse` rows and the cost-support transfers carry. It is minted once and never reused, so a removed recipient's history stays resolvable forever.

name.description: The organisation's registered name, as published. Money rows name organisations, never persons (URS ENG-083).

country.description: The country of registration as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. A code rather than a name because the two facts that hang on it are jurisdictional: whether the organisation may lawfully receive a transfer from a Swiss association under the law that applies to it (statutes Art. 7(2) item 2), and which sanctions regimes the screening must clear and whether it is seated in a jurisdiction the FATF calls for action on (item 3). The rendering surface prints the country's name from the code.

category.description: The one category of the seven this organisation is assigned to (D33 item 1). One category per recipient: a basket is made of recipients, not of shares of a recipient.

shareBps.description: This recipient's share OF ITS CATEGORY's amount, in basis points. The shares of one category's active recipients sum to exactly 10000 — apportioned by the same largest-remainder rule with the same list-order tiebreak, so three equal recipients read 3333 / 3333 / 3334 rather than three rounded thirds that lose a unit. JSON Schema cannot express a sum across items, so the bound is stated here rather than left as a surprise, exactly as `purpose-yml.v1` states its micro-share bound. Zero is valid for a recipient that is listed but not yet active.

website.description: The organisation's website, where it has one. Optional: a published website is no longer a condition of listing (D33 item 2(g) is superseded by statutes Art. 7(2)), and a newly founded organisation may not have one yet.

address.description: The organisation's postal address, where it publishes one. Optional: a published address is no longer a condition of listing (D33 item 2(g) is superseded by statutes Art. 7(2)).

registrationRef.description: The reference of the register entry or official record that shows the organisation's legal form as a not-for-profit organisation under the law of its country (statutes Art. 7(2) item 1) — the register's own identifier, so a reader can open it. The public list carries it beside the legal form; a newly founded organisation is not excluded.

standard.description: The evidence held in the recipient file for the floor of statutes Art. 7(2) and for the checks the Recipient Rules set. The Association keeps one file per recipient — registration, foreign-receipt evidence, screening records, grant letter, receipts, and accounts where they exist — and these are references into it. The members keep their D33 item 2 names; what they evidence is the floor and the Rules.

accountsYears.description: Years of published accounts, where the organisation has any — a recorded fact, never a condition of listing. Statutes Art. 7(2) sets no minimum and a newly founded organisation is not excluded, so zero is valid and the member is optional; the former minimum of three (D33 item 2(a)) no longer applies.

foreignReceiptEvidence.description: The evidence that the organisation may lawfully receive a transfer from a Swiss association under the law that applies to it — for instance a foreign-contribution registration (statutes Art. 7(2) item 2). One foreign-funding regime per recipient country is a cost the decision accepted with its eyes open.

screening.description: The sanctions screening records for statutes Art. 7(2) item 3 — not the target of sanctions that apply to the Association, not seated in a jurisdiction the FATF calls for action on: the SECO, EU, UN and OFAC lists, checked as the Recipient Rules set, each check recorded. All four lists appear — hence at least four entries — and the array grows with every later check rather than being overwritten.

result.description: A `hit` is a removal for cause under D33 item 3: it takes effect at once, is published with its ground, and the entry carries `removedAt` and `removalGround`. The value exists in the enum because a screening result that cannot be recorded is a screening nobody can audit.

ref.description: The recorded check in the recipient file.

independenceDeclared.description: The declaration for statutes Art. 7(2) item 4: the organisation is not controlled by any member, board member, employee or contractor of the Association, or by a person close to one, and gives no such person a personal benefit. Enforced as a constant because a listing without the declaration is not a listing the statutes permit; where a link short of control exists, the person concerned is excluded from the vote (Art. 68 ZGB) and the fact is published in `declaredConflict`. The wider D33 item 2(d) limbs — no contributor or repository owner among its officers, no financial link to any of them — are no longer requirements.

declaredConflict.description: The published fact where a link exists, together with the exclusion it caused (statutes Art. 7(2) item 4; Art. 68 ZGB).

bankTransferOnly.description: Statutes Art. 7(2) item 5: paid only into a bank account in the organisation's own name that the Association has verified — by bank transfer, never in cash and never in crypto-assets. A constant, because this is not a per-recipient preference — it is the payment rail the statutes allow.

grantLetterRef.description: The one-page grant letter stating the unrestricted purpose within the organisation's category, which the organisation accepts — a practical step under the Recipient Rules, not a test a newly founded organisation cannot meet.

annualStatementRef.description: A light yearly check the Recipient Rules may ask for — a short statement or a published annual report. A practical step, never a condition of listing.

receiptsRef.description: Where the per-transfer receipts are held. The receipt for one transfer travels on that transfer's own row (`cost-support.v1`).

activeFrom.description: The first month this recipient receives under. Additions are prospective, after thirty days' public notice (D33 item 3).

activeTo.description: The last month this recipient receives under, once an end is known. Absent means active with no end recorded.

removedAt.description: When a removal for cause took effect — at once, not at a month boundary (D33 item 3).

removalGround.description: The published ground for a removal for cause: for instance a sanctions hit or loss of registration. Published WITH the removal — a recipient that disappears without a stated ground is exactly the fact this list exists to prevent. The removed recipient's share for that month goes to the other recipients of its category, and nothing is ever clawed back from what was already transferred (D33 items 3 and 4).

sample.description: True in a sample dataset, on every entry, alongside a name that says so. A production list carries no `sample` entry: sample data is labelled sample, and no surface renders a fixture as a listed organisation.
